quote: The study was an open, parallel group design conducted in oral surgery outpatients. The subjects were 15 young (mean age 22.5 years), healthy (ASA class I) men (n=9) and women (n=6) who were free of allergy to any of the test medications.
proposed_wording: A textbook figure from 1984 with no trial deriving it; later reviews state plainly that scientific evidence supporting this dose is lacking. Clinical studies around and above that amount do exist - in patients with cardiovascular disease, haemodynamic measurement by impedance cardiography (Niwa 2001), a double-blind crossover trial with plasma epinephrine (Davenport 1990), blood pressure and heart rate in treated hypertension after an amount above the figure (Meechan 1997) and a randomised trial with 24-hour monitoring in coronary artery disease (Neves 2007); and, in young healthy oral-surgery patients with no cardiac patients included, plasma-epinephrine and haemodynamic measurement after an amount above the figure (Troullos 1987, n = 15) - but none establishes the figure as a threshold.
